messages:
mike: starting a terraform import of the eu-gpu-pool into prod workspace, CI died on the final step with a backend lock.
ana: seeing the same, infra-ci job 321 failed with 'lock held by 1945610000' from GCS backend.
julia: ugh GCS locks again. are we running a concurrent apply? who kicked off an apply in prod?
mike: I triggered a targeted import to move resources from project:gpu-mig to project:gpu-pools — should've been quick, didn't expect a global lock.
chris: infra-ci shows a concurrent run from branch/migrate-gpu at 1945611000, maybe two people ran imports.
julia: ops-oncall-bot: can you confirm who has the lock and TTL?
ops-oncall-bot: Lock held by run: infra-ci#321 (user:mike) since 1945610990. TTL expires in ~4m.
nana: TTL not clearing, job is hung. terraform force-unlock fails with "state altered remotely" when I try.
mike: paste of the error log:
```
Error: Provider produced inconsistent final plan

Releasing lock failed: storage.Objects.Update: preconditionFailed
Lock ID: infra-ci#321
```
ana: looks like the GCS object lease got clobbered by a concurrent gsutil rewrite.
chris: We also noticed some VPC routes in the imported resources point to a peering that no longer exists — likely cause of plan inconsistencies.
julia: proposal: abort the stuck run, manually copy the statefile to a safe location, run `terraform state pull` to inspect, then do a targeted `terraform state rm` for the stale peering resources before force-unlocking.
mike: agree but we should avoid deleting resources accidentally. I'll snapshot the bucket: `gsutil cp gs://redwood-terraform/prod.tfstate gs://redwood-state-backups/prod-1945623456.tfstate`
nana: after snapshot, try: `terraform state rm module.vpc.google_compute_network_peering.peer_to_old` then `terraform force-unlock 1945610990` from a local terraform client.
chris: if state rm isn't enough, we may need to `terraform state mv` the gpu pool into a new partial statefile and import to a fresh workspace to avoid cross-module drift.
julia: strong +1 for splitting the state. long term we should stop having the gpu pool in the same state as the global VPC; it causes these cross-domain failures.
mike: doing the snapshot now, pausing other CI triggers for prod. will post when snapshot is complete.
ops-oncall-bot: CI triggers for workspace 'prod' have been muted by mike until 1945623750.
nana: snapshot finished. attempting `terraform state rm module.vpc.google_compute_network_peering.peer_to_old` in a screen session now.
mike: state rm succeeded, now running `terraform force-unlock 1945610990`
chris: unlock succeeded, infra-ci job 321 shows unlocked but subsequent plan still errors on "peering does not exist" because remote project was rewired.
julia: next step: create a new workspace 'prod-gpu-split', `terraform state pull > prod.tfstate`, then `terraform state mv module.gpu_pool module.gpu_pool` into the new workspace file and `terraform import` the GPU instances there.
mike: I'll open a PR with the workspace split automation and a one-time migration runbook. tagging infra-ci to run a dry-run.
infra-ci: triggered pipeline 322 (dry-run) for branch: feature/split-gpu-state.
nana: monitoring 322 logs — looks clean so far, no lock conflict and plan shows only gpu_pool changes.
julia: follow-up action items: 1) add TTL alert if GCS lock TTL > 10m, 2) add guard in CI to prevent concurrent imports on prod, 3) schedule state split for other big resources.
mike: I'll write the runbook and add the CI guard. thanks everyone for quick responses. :thumbsup:
